prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of a dark dining table sloping away from the camera wearer from roughly 0.4 m at the bottom edge to 1.2 m at the top edge, with the wearer's left and right hands in the bright foreground (0.2–0.5 m) and several other diners' hands and arms around the table perimeter (0.5–1.1 m away and 0.2–0.6 m from each other). In front of the wearer within arm's reach (0.4–0.8 m) sit a square plate below two central bowls (0.15 m apart), a glass and napkin holder to their left, small bowls on the far left, and another diner's plate and utensils on the right, while all people's heads and upper torsos are cropped out of view so their facing and gaze directions cannot be seen directly (though arm angles show the wearer faces the table while others face inward from the left, top, and right). Across the five frames, the bright foreground left arm (either the wearer's or a left-side neighbor's) reaches forward and right in frame 2 to about 0.6 m, occluding the square plate and left central bowl before retreating to the bottom-left edge in frames 3–5, while a hand from the top-right reaches down in frame 5 to about 0.6 m over the right central bowl, partially occluding the table edge. Compared to the dimly lit RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the dark sleeves and hands in the bottom-right and far-left from the black background and highlights the 3D rim concavities of the bowls. However, the depth map is unreliable on small or specular tableware—such as the candle and glass on the upper left and the metal fork and spoon on the square plate, which flatten into the tabletop plane—and creates blurry depth bleeding around the reaching arm in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map partitions the scene into a central dining table surface (~0.4–1.2 m from the camera wearer) surrounded by overlapping person regions representing the camera wearer's hands at the bottom (0.3–0.5 m) and neighboring diners' arms on the left, top, and right (0.5–1.1 m away, spaced 0.2–0.6 m apart), though all heads and gazes remain out of frame above and behind the viewport boundaries. Within arm's reach of both the wearer and the surrounding diners (0.4–0.8 m), the map detects the left central bowl, the adjacent glass and napkin holder (labeled as cup), the food on the foreground square plate (labeled as pizza in frames 1–2), and utensils (labeled as fork, spoon, or knife) held by the wearer's right hand or resting on the plate. Across the five frames, a large purple person mask extends from the left in frame 2 to reach the central bowl (occluding the table and plate below it) before retreating left in frames 3–5, while the top-right person mask expands downward across the right side of the table in frame 5 as an arm approaches the right bowl. The segmentation map makes the boundary between the dark-clothed arms at the right/top edges and the dark room background much easier to see than in the low-light RGB frames. However, it is highly unreliable and temporally inconsistent: it completely misses the right central bowl in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 and the left small bowls in frames 3–5, fragments the dining table and people into shifting multi-colored masks with black unsegmented holes, and mislabels the napkin holder as a cup and the wearer's reaching arm or held utensils as separate person instances.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background for a few limbs over the table (~0.3–0.9 m from the camera wearer), completely omitting the table layout, dishes, and most of the surrounding people's bodies and heads (leaving facing direction and eye gaze undetermined beyond the inward orientation of the detected forearms). In frame 1, a yellow body-skeleton structure tracks the camera wearer's raised left arm and hand in the left foreground (~0.3 m away, within immediate reach of the glass and bowls), while in frames 2 and 3 magenta hand skeletons appear for the wearer's left hand at the bottom-left (~0.4 m), the wearer's right hand holding utensils (~0.45 m, 0.25 m to the right), and a top diner's hand reaching from above (~0.8 m away in frame 3). Across the sequence, the pose detections shift sporadically as hands move: the wearer's left hand drops from the upper-left in frame 1 to the bottom-left in frames 2–3 as it retreats, disappears completely in frame 4 despite remaining visible in RGB, and in frame 5 only the top-right diner's downward-reaching arm and hand (~0.6 m away, within arm's reach of the right bowl and the wearer's right hand) are tracked with overlapping yellow and magenta keypoints. Where present, the magenta finger skeletons in frames 2, 3, and 5 reveal exact finger articulation and grip posture in dim areas that are hard to distinguish in the RGB strip. Nevertheless, the pose map is severely unreliable across all five frames: it misses the majority of visible hands (including the right-side neighbor's hands in all frames, the reaching left arm in frame 2, and all hands in frame 4) and hallucinates miniaturized full-body yellow torso-and-limb skeletons onto single forearms and hands in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5.
